findings.title: Post-handshake response errors are swallowed into a non-retryable unknown via bare except
findings.issue: The transport wraps the entire request/response handling (including response reading, size/type checks, and json parsing after a successful connection close) in `except Exception: raise StorageError('speech outcome unknown; automatic retry denied')`. A definitively rejected/invalid provider response (e.g., HTTP error before any audio was processed, or a malformed reply after a completed request) is indistinguishable from a true unknown outcome and forces the operation permanently unretryable, wasting budget and blocking legitimate retries on clear failures.
findings.fix: Distinguish pre-send/timeout/unknown transport failures (fail closed, no retry) from definitive HTTP status codes or post-ack validation failures; only convert indeterminate transport errors to non-retryable unknown, and surface explicit provider rejections as ordinary failures without consuming the durable attempt fence when safe.

findings.title: Duplicate settle path can double-charge budget or mark accepted over unknown
findings.issue: `execute_reserved_groups` calls `settle(...)` for each prepared operation in the success path, but `settle()` allows transition from states `prepared`/`accepted`/`unknown` and, when `op['actual'] is None`, will recompute the window charge on a second call if the operation is already `accepted`/`unknown` (it does not return early for those states when `actual is None`). A retry or observer-driven `settle(...)` after `execute_reserved`/`execute_reserved_groups` already settled (e.g., usage callback in `composition.scoped_client`) can double-decrement `reserved` or double-increment `consumed`, or
findings.fix: Make `settle` strictly idempotent: only transition from `prepared` exactly once and treat any subsequent call (with identical or absent `actual`) as a no-op, raising `StateConflict` only on conflicting `actual` values.

not_verified: Runtime composition/archive and network-blocked native report path were read but not executed; end-to-end behavior of `RuntimeArchiveTransport` error classification and `scoped_client` usage-observer/
Actual concurrency behavior of `pa_policy` table constraints and transaction isolation under simultaneous `settle` calls was not test
Full live provider behavior (OpenAI/Graph/Brave) remains synthetic-only as designed; no human/deep-role approval assessment performed.
findings.summary: Implementation shows strong fail-closed and durable-fence design overall, but two concrete P1 defects remain: speech/vision transport error handling collapses definitive post-response failures into a non-retryable unknown, and the shared `settle` routine is not idempotent for `actual=None`, allowing double-charging or state overwrite on redundant settlement paths (notably the usage observer invoked after `execute_reserved*` has already settled). These should be fixed before broader rollout to avoid budget corruption and unnecessary permanent task-fencing on clearly failed requests.
